A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MineDraft. All 23 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including appendices, are readable. Text, equations, figures, and tables support comparison across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original throughput, latency, verification-success-rate, and profiling results across multiple model configurations and four datasets.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds GPU-normalized results, communication-overhead measurements, and parallelization-coverage statistics.

M1.justification: The two-batch execution, assignment and recycling rules, fallback mechanism, and KV-allocation scheduler patch remain unchanged. Adaptive scheduling and request-dependent drafting are discussed as future work, not implemented method changes.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same generation tasks on Arena, ShareGPT, Spec-Bench, and Tough. The large MoE experiment already appears in v1. Added analyses examine retained workloads rather than introducing new datasets or test scenarios.

E2.justification: v2 Fig. 17 adds matched standard SD plus TETRIS throughput/latency controls for extra-token counts 1–3 in Setting 1; these controls are absent from v1's corresponding comparisons in Figs. 3 and 10. The principal SD, PEARL, and EAGLE comparator families remain.

E3.justification: Sections 6.4/C.5 introduce GPU-normalized evaluation: throughput is divided by GPU count and parallel-method latency multiplied by 1.25. New analyses measure communication fractions and parallel-step coverage. Setting 7's stated drafter changes from EAGLE-Vicuna-33B to EAGLE-Vicuna-13B. These are reported evaluation changes; the PDFs do not establish reruns of retained experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds extra-token performance sensitivity, draft-size VSR comparisons, communication-overhead diagnosis, and quantitative tail-effect analysis in Fig. 17, expanded Fig. 16, and Tables 1–2. Existing VSR-trimming analyses remain. The additional sequence-count plots in v1 Figs. 18–19 are removed.

E5.justification: The general three-trial mean/standard-deviation practice and two-trial MoE exception remain. New Table 1 explicitly reports one profiling run; Table 2 presents three-run averages without dispersion values. These are limited reporting additions, not evidence of increased repetitions for existing results.

E6.justification: New normalized results report gains up to 40.55% in throughput and 24.38% in latency over standard SD, alongside 2.08% worse normalized latency on Spec-Bench in Setting 2. Tables 1–2 add communication measurements and 99.19% average parallelization coverage. Additional control/VSR results appear, while v1 Figs. 18–19 disappear. Retained raw headline results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4 corrects E[T] from R f(t) to R/f(t). Appendix B repairs timing expressions and missing R factors and replaces Lemma 2's proof with a piecewise monotonicity argument. Theorem 1 narrows from all alpha*V above approximately 1.68 to alpha*V approximately 1.68, with an approximate rather than strict 1.59 factor.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the batch-parallel framework, vLLM plugin, extra-GPU requirement, and headline 75% throughput/39% latency claims. The broad 37% theoretical-contribution wording also remains, despite the formal theorem revision assessed under T1.

C2.justification: v2 explains small-k normalized-latency failures through communication overhead and interprets measured parallelization coverage as making the tail effect negligible. Appendix A adds workload-saturation, oversized-batch, and request-difficulty limitations. The new Impact Statement qualifies energy benefits as deployment-dependent. Earlier imbalance and batch-exhaustion limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 revises the reported hardware from L40 to L40S, clarifies four-versus-five-GPU comparison allocations, and corrects draft-model naming, including the MoE caption's Qwen3-13B to Qwen3-14B. Software versions, default generation settings, and the disclosed code repository remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds AdaEDL, MagicDec, and references by Fernandez and Gunther to support limitations and scalability discussion. SpecServe/AdaSpec and several publication updates refer to retained works. The central positioning as complementary to drafting optimizations remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition remains, with localized wording and terminology edits. Experimental subsections are reorganized, limitations move to Appendix A, and acknowledgements, an Impact Statement, and updated affiliation/proceedings text appear. This is a limited restructuring rather than an extensive rewrite.

P2.justification: v2 adds normalized-result displays and two tables, expands ablation panels, and substantially reorganizes experimental figures. Latency panels move between the main text and appendix, sequence/batch-size plots are merged, and captions and panel labels are revised. Many underlying plots are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: GPU normalization, added diagnostics, and more specific limitations make v2's efficiency evidence more informative. Equation corrections and the improved Lemma 2 proof also help, although some sequence-count evidence is dropped. The overall gain remains limited: Appendix B still incorrectly identifies a decreasing function's minimum at the lower boundary, and broad 37% wording remains despite the narrowed theorem.
